# Chapter One: The Noise in the Dark

> *"Survival out on the fringe isn't about being the strongest. It's about outlasting the ghosts that follow you into the dark."*

The synthetic bourbon at the Rusty Anchor tasted like refined rocket propellant and stale copper, but at four credits a glass, Gracie Campbell wasn't in the mood to complain.

It had been ninety days since she had tumbled out of that automated trash scow onto the rusted scrap heaps of the Outer Rim. Ninety days of nursing septic fever in abandoned cargo containers, stealing black-market antibiotics, and learning what it felt like to share a skull with an unhinged ghost.

Freeport 9 hung in the hollowed-out belly of a dead nickel-iron asteroid at the outer lip of the Orion Spur, bathed in the sickly amber glow of flickering sodium lamps and sputtering plasma conduits. The air here was recycled so many times it carried the persistent tang of sulfur, grease, and cheap tobacco. It was an outlaw sanctuary, a place where mercenaries, deserters, and drifters went when they ran out of planets to flee to.

It was exactly where Gracie wanted to be.

Beneath her dark trenchcoat, she kept her posture relaxed, but her senses were wired taut. Across her occipital bone, the Box hummed with a low, cold vibration that sent faint static tingling through her teeth.

*He's looking at us,* the raspy voice whispered in her auditory nerve. *The bartender. Look at his left cuff. A syringe. He's working for Vengeance. Shoot him. Draw both guns and shoot him between the eyes before he pumps the gas!*

Gracie closed her eyes for half a second, breathing through her nose. *Shut up,* she thought back. *He's eighty years old and wiping a sticky counter with a dirty rag. He doesn't know who Vengeance is, and he doesn't care who I am.*

*You're blind!* the voice hissed, panicked and acidic. *They're everywhere! The needles never stop!*

“One more glass,” Gracie said aloud, her voice cool and measured as she slid an aluminum credit token across the stained wood.

The old barkeep poured the murky amber liquid without looking up. “You got someone waiting on you, kid. Booth six. Shady character in a corporate cowl.”

*Ambush!* the voice shrieked. *Drop a grenade through the ventilation grate! Burn the whole tavern!*

Gracie ignored the scream, picked up her glass, and turned toward booth six. A thin man in a dust-stained gray trenchcoat sat with his hands flat on the table.

“Captain Campbell,” the man said smoothly.

“Just Campbell,” Gracie corrected, sliding into the opposite bench. “Or Gracie, if you’re polite. What’s the job?”

“A salvage contract. In the Obsidian Nebula.” The man slid a holocron across the scarred metal. “A precursor dreadnought, adrift since the First Interstellar Accord. Five kilometers of cold, unlooted alloy. My employers want the core. You bring it back, you get half a million credits.”

*He's lying!* the Box yelled. *It's a death trap! Look at his pulse—he's bait! Shoot his fingers off!*

Gracie leaned forward, her cybernetically augmented eyes scanning the holocron's telemetry. The coordinates were genuine. The radiation signatures matched precursor void-drift.

“Who else knows about this wreck?” she asked quietly.

“Nobody,” the broker smiled.

*A lie!* the Box rasped. *Baron Vargas has the same frequency! I remember that encryption... Vengeance sold that cipher to Vargas eighty years ago!*

Gracie’s heart hitched. For once, beneath the hysterical paranoia, the passenger’s century of captive knowledge held a grain of terrifying truth. 

Before she could speak, heavy magnetic boots clomped on the metal grating behind her.

“Well, well,” a rough voice boomed. “If it ain’t Blake Campbell’s runaway brat. The Black Sun Cartel pays fifty thousand just for your head, little girl.”

*KILL THEM!* the Box screamed, blinding her right eye with flashing crimson static. *BLOW THE REACTOR! DIE BEFORE THEY STRAP US DOWN!*

Gracie didn't blow anything. She ducked sideways as a heavy slug slammed into the wooden backrest where her head had rested a fraction of a second earlier. In a smooth, fluid blur honed by months of running, she drew her left plasma pistol, kicked the table into the bounty hunter’s shins, and fired a blue kinetic bolt into his sternum, sending him sprawling into the corridor.

“Business is concluded,” Gracie told the terrified broker, snatching the holocron. “Tell your employers *The Starlight Drifter* accepts the contract.”
